changeability.rationale: The important cross-cutting concerns (sprites, card rendering, API base, caching) each funnel through one obvious place, so most fixes are one-edit. A few small duplicated expressions (card assembly on the home page, query building, `MISSING`, effect fallback) mean some fixes land twice, but everything is easy to find.

evidence: app/lib/api.ts:1 and app/lib/data.ts:1 — `import "server-only"` prevents client code from reaching the data layer
app/lib/data.ts:44-52 — `CardData` is a narrow, serializable interface; `cardsForPokemon`'s optional `extra` callback is a clean seam for per-context card variations
app/components/Section.tsx:4, app/components/PokemonCards.tsx:8, app/components/MoveTable.tsx:53 — components are purely prop-driven presentational units
app/components/Filters.tsx:1, GameSelect.tsx:1, MoveTable.tsx:1 — the only client components, and their only coupling is `next/navigation` and props
app/lib/format.ts:1 — shared server/client helpers kept deliberately free of server imports
coupling.rationale: Server and client code are separated by explicit `"use client"` boundaries and `server-only` guards; every component consumes narrow, serializable interfaces; no shared mutable state and no component reaches into another's internals. This is the codebase's strongest property.

evidence: app/lib/data.ts:52-70 — `cardsForPokemon` handles the real variation in the app (three card contexts with different inputs, alternate-form exclusion, dex ordering) via one helper and an `extra` callback rather than flags
app/components/MoveTable.tsx:39 — `showLevel` flag matches genuine variation (level-up vs other method tables), not accreted creep

app/app/pokemon/[name]/page.tsx:31-40, app/app/moves/[name]/page.tsx:13-21, app/app/abilities/[name]/page.tsx:10-18, app/app/types/[name]/page.tsx:20-28 — the fetch/metadata/not-found page skeleton is copy-pasted four times; a new Items resource means a fifth copy
app/components/TypeBadge.tsx:4 — `link`/`size` props are small and match real usage differences (cards vs badges vs filters)
abstraction_design.rationale: The shared primitives (api client, format helpers, Section, PokemonCards, TypeBadge, cardsForPokemon) stretch to new cases without modification, and flag parameters reflect real variation. The one design gap is the per-resource page boilerplate, which is duplicated rather than factored — though for thin Next.js route files that's near-idiomatic and abstracting it further would risk over-engineering.

findings.issue: The home page builds `CardData` objects inline instead of reusing `cardsForPokemon`, duplicating card assembly in two places
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared card-assembly helper (or give `cardsForPokemon` an index-entry variant) so card construction — sprite URL, humanized label, dedupe — has a single definition

findings.issue: The home page's query-string shape is constructed in both `pageHref` here and `href` in `components/Filters.tsx:19-26`; adding or renaming a filter param requires coordinated edits in two files plus `onSelect`
findings.suggestion: Extract one shared `buildHomeUrl(params)` used by both the pagination links and the Filters component

findings.issue: Effect-fallback expression `english(...)?.short_effect ?? latestFlavorText(...) ?? "—"` is duplicated in the ability page
findings.suggestion: Add a `shortEffect(record)` helper to lib/format.ts (or a small lib helper) used by both pages
Import `MISSING` from lib/format.ts so the em-dash convention has one source

findings.issue: The `getX` + `generateMetadata` + `notFound` page skeleton is copy-pasted across four route files; new resources (e.g. Items) mean another copy
findings.suggestion: Factor a small per-resource loader + metadata helper (e.g. `loadResource(path, name)`) to cut the boilerplate per new page

findings.issue: Builds its own `typeLabels` map instead of using `getTypeLabels()` from lib/data.ts, a third way type labels get resolved
findings.suggestion: Reuse `getTypeLabels()` (or pass the labels already fetched via `getTypes()`) so label resolution has one implementation

findings.issue: `slug()` strips diacritics with a raw combining-character range (`/[̀-ͯ]/g`) that's fragile to read and easy to break when editing
findings.suggestion: Use an explicit unicode property escape (e.g. `/\p{Diacritic}/gu`) or drop diacritic stripping since headings here are ASCII

summary: This is a well-factored Next.js 16 app: server/client boundaries are explicit and enforced, components consume narrow serializable props, and the cross-cutting concerns (API client, caching, sprites, card rendering, formatting) each funnel through one obvious place, so most fixes are single-edit. The main editability cost is small-scale duplication — card assembly on the home page, home-page query building split between page and Filters, per-resource page boilerplate copied four times — which makes some changes land in two or three findable places rather than one. Against current stable Next.js 16.4 it uses the right contracts (async params, generateMetadata, force-dynamic) and would migrate to Cache Components cheaply since the cache is centralized.
